name: Xiaogang Hu
title: Professor; Dorothy Foehr Huck and J. Lloyd Huck Chair in Neurorehabilitation
department: Mechanical Engineering, Kinesiology, and Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation; Neuromechanics Laboratory
fitReason: Strong CS/AI and assistive-robotics fit through deep neural decoding, representation learning, cross-day adaptation and continuous prosthetic control. Current Penn State role is verified, with an active methods pipeline rather than reliance on former UNC affiliation.

physicalEvidence.summary: The full 2025 IEEE THMS paper implements a trained, subject-calibrated parallel CNN that maps high-density surface EMG features to finger-specific neural drive, then uses regression/Kalman filtering to command an actual i-Limb hand’s index, middle and ring finger forces. Reference forces update at 8 Hz and the conventional PD/motor controller at 32 Hz. Ten neurologically intact participants performed isometric tasks; the paper separately documents the physical hand setup and supplemental demonstration. It does not claim ten independent clinical prosthesis deployments. Thumb/object manipulation and validation in people with motor disabilities remain future work. The manuscript was received in July 2024 and uses UNC-Chapel Hill IRB approval with Penn State and UNC/NC State authors. Exact experiment dates, campus location and present apparatus ownership are unverified, so this is collaborative/older execution evidence, not a new 2026 Penn State-owned deployment. Current 2026 cross-day decoding publications establish ongoing methods research but are not counted as additional hardware execution.

shortVisit.summary: Current official Penn State endowed professorship and lab leadership are verified. The live Positions page invites PhD, postdoctoral and undergraduate candidates, but no applicable outside-master visitor offer. Current lab institutional visitor feasibility is kept separate from faculty availability.
